$description: Snapshot of the LIVE SAMAVESH Figma library — fileKey 3FF5l0SMNIwdpZrKkeyPTm, the canonical one named in GOVERNANCE.md. TWO OLDER COPIES still exist and still contain variables (qyzTEy8… 261 vars, T3bkN5g… 176), so a sync run against either looks successful and reaches nobody: check the count before writing. Variable names ARE the canonical DTCG paths, so this file doubles as the proof that the Figma tree and the source tree are the same tree.
$note: 2026-08-11, NINTH pass — the layout system, and the tap-target ladder. 9 variables added to Space (now 85; library 909). GRID: 12 columns and a 24px gutter, which is UX4G 3.0 / Bootstrap exactly, because UX4G is the Government of India's own system and this repo holds a parity contract with it — a designer moving between the two libraries must not find a different grid. What is NOT UX4G's is the SHAPE: UX4G expresses its grid as Bootstrap CSS classes, which is precisely why none of it had ever reached Figma and why a designer had nothing to bind a layout grid to. These are tokens instead, following IBM Carbon's model. Page margin is responsive (16 / 24 / 32px) rather than Bootstrap's flat 12px half-gutter, because 12px either side of a government page on a 1280px desktop is too thin — Carbon uses 32px and GOV.UK 30px. TARGET: a ladder, not one number. 44px is WCAG 2.5.5, which is Level AAA and NOT the AA floor it is usually quoted as; the AA floor is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 at 24 by 24 CSS px, with a spacing exception. GIGW 3.0 binds this estate to WCAG 2.1 AA + IS 17802, and WCAG 2.1 AA contains NO target-size criterion at all, so every value here is a deliberate choice above the mandate rather than a compliance minimum. min=24 (2.5.8 AA), comfortable=44 (2.5.5 AAA and Apple 44pt), spacious=48 (Material 3, 48dp), spacing=8 (Material separation, and what makes the 2.5.8 spacing exception reachable). NOT added, and why. The breakpoint group was NOT extended to UX4G's six: those three are the fluid TYPE ramp's clamp anchors (the generator throws without mobile and desktop), not layout media queries, so a layout breakpoint set is a separate axis and a separate decision. container/2xl (1320px) was not added because the estate's content width is 1280px, so a wider container would contradict it. Shadow and elevation still have NO Figma representation and cannot have one as variables: Figma holds only COLOR / FLOAT / STRING / BOOLEAN and a shadow is composite — it needs effect STYLES. TENTH pass — elevation reached Figma, as effect STYLES rather than variables (a shadow is composite; variables cannot hold one). Six elevation/* created from shadow.* exactly. The claim in the ninth pass that designers had NO shadow tokens was WRONG: six Shadows/shadow-* effect styles already existed, unknown to the code — and not one of them matches the token source. All six use flat #212121 against the tokens' tinted rgb(31,36,40), and shadow-s and shadow-md also differ in geometry. They were left untouched and annotated rather than corrected, because they are applied in consumer files this library cannot enumerate. ELEVENTH pass — the six Focus States/* effect styles had no description at all (found by the coverage check after the elevation work) and now have one each. They are otherwise the healthiest thing in the library: every colour is variable-BOUND to color/transparent/<family>/48, so unlike the Shadows/* they cannot rot into a literal. One thing worth knowing and now written down: each is a single flush 4px spread, while the build renders a 2px ring held 2px off the control — same 4px footprint, no transparent gap, because a drop shadow cannot leave one without painting the backdrop. Recorded as a limitation, not as drift to fix. Effect-style description coverage is now 18/18.  TWELFTH pass — the functional and neutral ramps, VALUES ONLY: 62 Palette variables re-valued in both Blue and Navy, plus 42 Color descriptions whose published contrast measurement moved with them. Nothing created, nothing renamed, nothing deleted — every collection count is unchanged (Palette 164, Color 472) and the Palette modes are still exactly [Blue, Navy], asserted by the push script itself before it wrote anything, because dbim is code-only by standing instruction. What changed: dangerScale, warningScale, infoScale and neutralScale, the four ramps the 2026-08-11 rebuild had not reached. The reason it mattered to the LIBRARY and not only to the code is that bg/status/error/bolder and bg/status/warning/bolder were published carrying the sentence 'BELOW the 4.5:1 implied by the bolder rung' — a Figma library telling designers, correctly, that two of its own filled buttons could not hold their own text. They now read 'meets 4.5:1: text-safe (WCAG 1.4.3 AA)' at 6.68:1 and 5.68:1, and there is no such sentence left anywhere in the library. The descriptions were pushed WITH the values deliberately: a values-only push would have left 42 variables publishing a measurement that was true of colours the file no longer contains, which is the exact failure the prominence contract exists to prevent. Everything else in Palette was verified already in sync before writing, so the 62 are the whole diff. TWELFTH pass — the library was reconciled with the merged code at VALUE level, which the name checksums had never covered. 13 component tokens were bound to the wrong palette rung (cmp/action/destructive/primary/* still on danger 700/800/900 after the code moved to 600/700/800; cmp/action/brand/tonal/* still on primary 100/200/300, stale since v0.13.0), ref/font/family/mono still held the webfont the code had reverted, 12 font size/lineHeight variables were unlinked literals where the payload declares aliases into Space, and 54 fluid-type variables carried the OLD tablet curve. All pushed. Seven of eight collections are now byte-identical to the payload; the eighth differs only in ref/font/weight/*, deliberately — see $valueChecksums.knownDifference. Recorded as checksums rather than a value dump, because 1,400 mirrored values would rot on their own. THIRTEENTH pass — the last value difference is closed, and it was closed in the EXPORTER, not the library. ref/font/weight/* projected CSS numbers (400/500/600/700) into a payload whose live counterparts are STRING font-STYLE names (Regular/Medium/SemiBold/Bold), because Figma has no numeric weight — a text style selects a cut by fontName.style. The library was already correct; the payload was the wrong side, which is why it could not be reconciled by pushing: resolvedType is fixed at creation. figma-variables.mjs now projects the full 100-900 ladder to style names, the same shape of fix as primaryFontFamily one axis over. ALL EIGHT collections are now byte-identical to the payload on values, and $valueChecksums.knownDifference is empty. THIRTEENTH pass — the chart palette's provenance. Nine Color variables: chart/cat/2 and chart/cat/3 repointed off retired brand colours (the old saffron #F97316 and Material green #2E7D32) onto India Green and — for cat/2 — secondaryScale/500 rather than the bright logo saffron, which measures 2.91:1 against the page and was the only one of the twelve under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1, and the seven chart/div/* converted from unlinked LITERALS into ALIASES onto the Palette collection. That last part is the same defect PR #52 found in the fluid-type variables, in a different corner: a diverging scale carrying its own copies of danger/neutral/success cannot follow them, and it had already drifted — negSoft and mid were copies of rungs taken before those ramps were rebuilt. Nothing created, nothing renamed; Color still 472 and Palette still 164, modes still [Blue, Navy]. The Color checksum was re-recorded only after a verified read returned the same value the build produces (6e10318e:472), which is the contract this record exists to hold. FOURTEENTH pass — the shadow ink. The five elevation/* effect styles were retinted from rgba(31,36,40) to rgba(30,33,36) and overlay/neutral/boldest with them: the shadow ramp claims in its own description to be tinted toward the body ink, and had been carrying a neutral/800 the 2026-08-11 rebuild moved. Geometry, alpha and blend mode untouched on every layer. The six Shadows/shadow-* styles were deliberately NOT touched — they are the pre-existing set on flat #212121 that has never matched the token source and is annotated as such, and Focus States/Neutral already reads rgba(30,33,36,0.48) because it is variable-bound to color/transparent/neutral/48 and tracked the rebuild on its own. One variable and five styles; nothing created, nothing renamed.

Every listed variable still occurs, so the ratchet in ghost-bindings-baseline.json remains correct — but boundOn counts are now overstated. Re-run the sweep for current figures.

$remediation.detail: fontSize/lineHeight rebound to value-identical ref/font/size/* and ref/font/lineHeight/*; letterSpacing (0.4px, no canonical token) and paragraphSpacing (inert on single-line text) unbound. Zero visual change.
$remediation.gap: Only covered authored, unstyled, non-instance text. Nodes inside components and nodes carrying a text style were skipped and still hold ghosts.

$remediation.detail: Font Size/6(24)->ref/radius/3xl · Font Size/11(56)->ref/space/6xl · Font Size/9(40)->ref/space/4xl · Font Size/10(48)->ref/space/5xl · Font Size/14(80)->ref/space/9xl. All exact value matches, zero visual drift.
$remediation.reach: Instances on 38 of 68 pages. Sampled after: Badges 94->4, Toggle 98->8, Avatars 116->8, Loader 94->8 (91-96% cleared per page).

$orphans.note: Variables that exist in the LIVE library but that the build payload does not define. Pre-existing drift, NOT created by a sync. Left in place deliberately: this is a PUBLISHED library, so a consumer binding cannot be enumerated from inside it and a delete is therefore unverifiable. Retire them only with evidence of zero consumers, and by RENAME to deprecated/* rather than deletion. They are also the ONLY 36 variables without codeSyntax, and one of them (border/neutral/inverse) still publishes the dead name var(--color-border-neutral-inverse) — deliberately not corrected, because the sync only touches what the source owns.

$incidents.what: RESOLVED — color/neutralScale/1100 was RENAMED in place, not deleted. No binding was detached.
$incidents.detail: A concurrent session recorded this as a hard delete with unrecoverable bindings. That was a reasonable reading of what it could see — the NAME was gone — but it is wrong, and the correction matters because "bindings are detached and cannot be restored" is alarming and false. What actually happened: the renumbering was applied as a two-step RENAME CHAIN (1000 -> 950 first to free the name, then 1100 -> 1000), which is the only safe way to renumber in a published library because renaming preserves the variable id and therefore every binding that points at it. Verified against the ids captured BEFORE the write: VariableID:3791:8969 (was 1000, #0a0d13) is now named color/neutralScale/950 and still exists; VariableID:3791:8970 (was 1100, #000000) is now named color/neutralScale/1000 and still exists. Both were re-read by id afterwards and both resolve. Nothing was created to replace them, so no id changed and no consumer lost its reference. The lesson is about OBSERVATION, not about the write: a missing NAME does not imply a missing VARIABLE, and the two can only be told apart by looking the id up directly.

$effectStyles.note: Effect styles, NOT variables. A shadow is a composite value and Figma variables hold only COLOR / FLOAT / STRING / BOOLEAN, so `shadow.*` and `elevation.*` can never be variables — an effect style is the only Figma primitive that fits. `elevation/*` is generated from `shadow.*` in src/primitive.json via build/shadow.mjs, and elevation-parity.test.mjs asserts these strings still match what that parser produces.

preExisting.note: Six `Shadows/shadow-*` effect styles predate the token sync and the code never knew about them. NONE of the six matches the token source: all use flat #212121 where the tokens use the tinted rgb(31,36,40), and shadow-s and shadow-md also differ in GEOMETRY, so a design using either does not match what ships. They were NOT changed — this is a published library and they are applied in consumer files, so altering their geometry would restyle other people's work unannounced. Each now carries a description naming the elevation/* style that supersedes it and the exact divergence. Retire them only with evidence of zero consumers.
preExisting.Shadows/shadow-xs: colour differs only — superseded by elevation/card
preExisting.Shadows/shadow-lg: colour differs only — superseded by elevation/modal
preExisting.Shadows/shadow-xl: colour differs only — superseded by elevation/toast
preExisting.Shadows/shadow-2xl: ORPHAN — no token behind it; the code ramp stops at shadow.xl

focus.note: Six `Focus States/*` effect styles. Unlike the shadows these are in GOOD shape — every one binds its colour to `color/transparent/<family>/48`, so they follow the brand and cannot rot into a literal. They shipped with no description at all, which is now fixed; each says which intent it belongs to and carries the geometry caveat below.
focus.geometryDivergence: Each style is a SINGLE FLUSH 4px spread. The build renders a 2px ring held 2px off the control (focus/width = ref/border/width/md = 2px, focus/offset = ref/space/xxs = 2px), so the total footprint agrees at 4px but the transparent gap does not exist in Figma. This is a LIMITATION, not drift to be fixed: a drop shadow cannot leave a transparent gap without painting the backdrop, and faking the gap means painting the inner 2px in the page colour — correct on the default surface and wrong on every other. Do not 'correct' these to two layers; the Figma ring is deliberately the heavier reading of the same affordance.

styles.Focus States/Primary - Active Shadow: bound to color/transparent/primary/48 — same value as the focus/ring token; the estate default

$valueChecksums.note: Per-collection checksum over `name|mode|value`, computed by build/figma-value-parity.mjs. The rest of this file records NAMES, and every check built on it compares names — which is why the library could hold 13 component tokens bound to the wrong palette rung, a reverted webfont, and 54 fluid-type variables carrying the old tablet curve, all under the correct names, with nothing noticing. `payload` is what the build produces; `figmaObserved` is a verified read of the library. They are expected to be EQUAL, and figma-value-parity.test.mjs fails when the payload moves without this record being refreshed.

knownDifference.$note: Recorded 2026-08-12. Every difference below is the ORPHAN set — variables that exist in the live library but that the build payload does not define. They are left in place deliberately (see $orphans): a published library cannot enumerate its consumers, so a delete is unverifiable. The arithmetic is exact, which is what makes this an explanation rather than an excuse — if either number moves by anything other than a whole orphan, the difference is real drift.
knownDifference.Palette: payload 280 entries vs library 328. The gap is exactly 48 = 24 Palette orphans x 2 modes (Blue, Navy). The orphans are border/neutral/inverse, focus/ring and 22 ref/color/* legacy names.
knownDifference.Type: payload 594 entries vs library 672. The gap is exactly 78 = 13 Type orphans x 6 modes (Website|Portal x Desktop|Tablet|Mobile). The orphans are the 10 deprecated/type/* variables, ref/font/family/body, ref/font/family/heading and ref/font/weight/displayMedium.
